split_question: Do you agree or disagree: the government should focus on supporting young people into work, education or training before it supports them through benefits?
angles: a guaranteed place, with a duty to take it up
an allowance first, with help alongside
local hubs run by mayors and councils, not Whitehall
facts_for_writers: The government says close to a million young people are not in education, employment or training, and describes the Youth Opportunities Unit as reporting directly to the Prime Minister. [s1]
The release gives no new cost figures; funding and implementation detail, including legislation, is to be set out in due course. [s1]
The Work and Pensions Secretary told the Commons the system spends 25 pounds on the consequences of inactivity for every pound it spends on opportunity. [s2]
Milburn recommends a youth allowance paid while a young person gets help from a Youth Opportunity Service; the statement presents this as a recommendation, not a government decision. [s2]

Existing spending named in the statement includes a 2.5 billion pound Youth Guarantee, and the Jobs Guarantee (a fully funded six-month job) is to open after 12 months on Universal Credit instead of 18. [s2]
